items.title: Don’t leave contract dentists behind after Budget 2027 doctor absorption, urges MDA
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) has urged the federal government and the Ministry of Health (MOH) to grant contract dental officers the same absorption opportunities as medical doctors and pharmacists, warning that trained dentists are being forced out of the public sector after their contracts lapsed without extension. In a statement today, MDA president Dr Chong Zhen Feng said the association welcomed the government’s commitment to reinforcing the public healthcare workforce, particularly the permanent appointment drive announced under Budget 2027. “In this regard, MDA respectfully calls upon the Government and MOH to accord similar consideration to contract dental officers, whose contributions to the nation’s public healthcare system are equally important,” the association said.

items.title: Man charged with murdering student in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN: An unemployed 19-year-old man was charged at the Kuantan magistrate's court today with murdering a female student. F. Alan Stevekumar was read the charge by a translator before magistrate Tuan Ruzuaini Tuan Lah. Wearing a black T-shirt and red shorts, Alan said "faham" (understand) after the charge was read.

items.title: Johor education department says daily closure notices are routine updates, don’t clash with state haze order
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 12 — The Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) will issue daily notifications on the extension of school closures due to the haze, despite the state government having announced a five-day extension yesterday. This follows JPNJ’s announcement today that all schools would be closed on Oct 12, while the state government had earlier announced that the closure would be extended until Oct 16, following the two-day closure on Oct 8 and 9. Meanwhile, JPNJ said the Year 4 Learning Matrix (MPT4) and other related assessments would be postponed and rescheduled in accordance with directives from the Examination Syndicate and JPNJ.

items.title: Police track down hit-and-run driver after fatal Jalan Kuching crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have tracked down the driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle crash that killed a five-year-old girl and injured two others on Jalan Kuching. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief, Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, said the accident involved five cars and a motorcycle during slow-moving traffic. Zamzuri said the girl's father sustained injuries to his right hand, while the 33-year-old Yamaha 135LC motorcyclist suffered head injuries.

items.title: A commitment to fiscal discipline and deficit reduction
items.summary: LETTER: The total of RM510 billion allocated for 2027 budget shows the government is really listening to the concerns of the people while also confronting great external challenges in the form of uncertain global economic outlook as well as the on-going Middle East crisis. The minimum wage raise to RM2,000 from RM1,700 is significant. Even workers pay in the middle of the range distribution has been push upward, where the starting wage benchmark for graduates and semi-skilled workers is set at RM2,500 a month.

items.title: Man hurt fleeing George Town EV battery storage blaze, firefighters bring flames under control
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 12 — A man was injured in a fire at an electric vehicle (EV) battery storage facility in Jalan Jelutong here yesterday. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said Eugene Chow Hao Jie, 31, sustained injuries while attempting to escape from the facility. “We received an emergency call at 3.42pm and immediately dispatched a fire engine from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene, where firefighters found a fire involving an EV battery storage facility measuring about 10 square feet.

items.title: Chin Hin Group launches sales gallery for RM814mil residential project in Segambut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Chin Hin Group Property (CHGP) has launched the sales gallery for Ophira Resort Residences, the company's latest nature-themed residential launch, offering a resort-inspired living experience. Set across 1.92 hectares of freehold land along Jalan Segambut, the serviced apartment development offers a harmonious sanctuary where nature meets the modern sophistication of Kuala Lumpur. Chang Tze Yoong, executive director and group chief executive officer of CHGP, said, Ophira Resort Residences reflects the company's vision of creating homes that go beyond the conventional boundaries of urban living.

items.title: Midnight crash near Glenmarie leaves two dead, five injured
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency distress call regarding the incident near the Glenmarie Industrial Park at 12.27am. “A total of 14 personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) and Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene. Ashrul Riezal said the Proton Wira was carrying four young men.

items.title: Marine police seize contraband cigarettes, liquor worth RM727k in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Marine police arrested two foreign men and seized 180,000 cigarettes and 7,860.64 litres of liquor worth RM727,351.71, including taxes, in Kubang Semang. The operation was conducted by the Marine Intelligence Unit of Marine Police Region One, Penang. Marine Police Region One commander, Assistant Commissioner Jaffri Bidin, said the raid followed intelligence on the alleged smuggling of liquor and untaxed cigarettes.

items.title: King Abdullah II arrives in Malaysia for two‑day state visit marking six decades of ties
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 12 — King Abdullah II of Jordan arrived in Malaysia yesterday for a two-day state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. This marks King Abdullah II’s second state visit to Malaysia since May 2008. During the visit, King Abdullah II will be accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara, followed by an audience with Sultan Ibrahim.

items.title: High car ownership drives Tuhu Car Care's Penang expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tuhu Car Care is expanding into Penang with the simultaneous opening of three stores, targeting a northern Malaysian market where car ownership is among the key drivers of demand for automotive maintenance and after-sales services. "Penang provides a significant market for automotive services," Vincent Chen, the company's regional head, said in a statement. He said the expansion beyond Kuala Lumpur also demonstrates the company's long-term commitment to making automotive services more accessible across the country.

items.title: Kota Tinggi records highest API reading at 170
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Kota Tinggi recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 170 this morning, as all eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy levels. Environment Department readings showed that Pasir Gudang recorded the state's second-highest API reading at 168, followed by Pengerang (164), Larkin (160), Tangkak (156), Batu Pahat and Kluang (152 each), and Segamat (129). PM2.5 was the dominant pollutant at all eight monitoring stations.

items.title: Anwar tells youths to lead now, urging students to be society’s conscience against corruption and injustice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said youths must embrace their role as leaders of the present, rather than wait for the future, urging university students to serve as the moral compass of society. He said young people must lead public discourse and boldly champion causes against corruption, exploitation and systemic injustice. “Why do you talk about future leaders?

items.title: Plantation earnings face 7pct hit from RM2,000 minimum wage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian plantation companies' earnings could fall by up to seven per cent in financial year 2028 (FY28) due to higher wages, partly offset by stronger crude palm oil (CPO) prices, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said. Analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang said the increase in the monthly minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027, would weigh on upstream plantation companies, particularly those with a higher proportion of general estate workers earning the minimum wage. Ng said the impact is likely to be more pronounced among upstream planters with Malaysian operations, including Johor Plantations Group Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd.

items.title: Police say Eric See-To released on bail after probe into online post mocking Quranic verse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Social media influencer ‘Lim Sian See’ was summoned to the Brickfields District Police Headquarters (IPD) yesterday to have his statement recorded over an online post. The source added that Lim was later released on police bail. In the post, Lim questioned the term before sarcastically linking it to another word.

items.title: RM69bil education allocation to bridge infrastructure gap, boost welfare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The nearly RM69 billion allocation received by the Education Ministry under the 2027 Budget aims to strengthen national education quality by upgrading school infrastructure and enhancing student and teacher welfare. The allocation includes RM2 billion to repair and maintain all types of schools and nearly RM1.3 billion to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, which is expected to bridge the educational facility gap, particularly in rural and remote areas. Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) Department of Social Sciences, Centre for General Studies and Co-Curricular senior lecturer Dr Nazreena Mohammed Yasin said the funding would help ensure students enjoy a safe and conducive learning environment regardless of location.

items.title: Girl, 5, killed after BYD Seal rear-ends Bezza in six-vehicle KL crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 5-year-old girl died while two others were injured in a six-vehicle crash along Jalan Kuching Saturday afternoon. The girl, who was in the rear passenger seat of a Perodua Bezza, died from severe head injuries while being taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 3.44pm crash involved five cars and a motorcycle.

items.title: Central banks face test. Will they be good cops or bond villains?
items.summary: LONDON: A standoff between central banks and their cash-strapped governments may well be looming as an intensifying bond market crunch reopens questions about the political independence of the banks well beyond their interest-rate policy. Central banks currently appear reluctant to rebuild holdings of sovereign debt, yet those holdings played a significant role in the swelling public borrowing over the past decade. If bond markets continue to tighten — as we've seen in recent weeks — political pressure on central banks to steady the ship will rise even further.

items.title: Special Branch cop makes fresh report with new evidence on alleged assault by border control chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — A Special Branch policeman who alleged he was assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has lodged a fresh report to submit new evidence. Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja’afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin confirmed that their client, 40-year-old Lance Corporal Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, lodged the supplementary report at the Sungai Besi police station on Oct 10, NST reported. The law firm alleged that Faiz and a second officer, Lance Corporal Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, who both serve as Travel Control Officers (TCO), were assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area, sustaining physical injuries and suffering humiliation.

items.title: KLIA Ekspres services disrupted by cable cut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KLIA Ekspres services were disrupted this morning following a cable cut between Putrajaya and Cyberjaya and Salak Tinggi stations. In a statement of Facebook, the operator said the combined train service would remain in effect until further notice. The operator said its technical team was working to rectify the issue and restore normal train services as soon as possible.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Healthcare access gap, Budget 2027 debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Government measures to address the gap in access to doctors, specialists and diagnostic facilities between urban hospitals and rural healthcare facilities will be among the key focuses of today’s Dewan Rakyat session. According to the Order of Business on the Parliament’s website, the issue will be raised by Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu), who will ask the Health Minister to explain the government’s measures to address the disparity during the question-and-answer session. This week’s Dewan Rakyat sitting will also see the start of the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, on Friday.

items.title: Ex-Bukit Besi assemblyman Roslee Daud dies at 66
items.summary: DUNGUN: Former Bukit Besi assemblyman Roslee Daud died early this morning. He served as Umno and Barisan Nasional's Bukit Besi assemblyman for two terms from May 2013 to August 2023. Funeral prayers will be held at Masjid Bukit Besi after Zohor prayers, followed by burial at the Bukit Besi Islamic Cemetery.

items.title: Merz Aesthetics steps up expansion amid aesthetics boom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Merz Aesthetics is strengthening its focus on Malaysia and the wider Asia-Pacific medical aesthetics market as the industry shifts towards skin longevity, personalised treatments and research-driven innovation. The global medical aesthetics company has launched a regional campaign featuring Hollywood actress Lucy Liu as its ambassador while planning a research and development innovation centre in Singapore to advance research into skin ageing and longevity. Industry research by MarketsandMarkets projects the regional medical aesthetics market to grow from US$3.75 billion in 2025 to US$8.66 billion by 2031, driven partly by demand for injectables and minimally invasive treatments.

items.title: Police intercept Isuzu Dmax after chase in Setiawangsa, seize machete, sickle, drugs and cable‑theft tools
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two local men arrested following a police chase along Jalan Wangsa 5, Bukit Antarabangsa heading towards the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) in Hulu Kelang here yesterday, were found to be in possession of sharp weapons, cable-theft equipment, and drugs inside their vehicle. Ampang Jaya District Police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said both suspects were apprehended when their Isuzu Dmax vehicle was intercepted at the junction of Jalan Jelatek and Jalan Taman Setiawangsa near the Caltex station in Setiawangsa. He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions, and Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958 for carrying or possessing offensive weapons in public places.

items.title: UK finance minister to call for big economies to get borrowing under control at IMF
items.summary: BANGKOK: British finance minister John Healey will stress the importance of budget discipline and improving resilience to geopolitical shocks when he meets his foreign counterparts on his first trip to the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings this week. Healey will argue that major economies need credible plans to get borrowing under control, the finance ministry said, following similar calls last week from IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. * Healey will meet Ukrainian Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko, among others, to discuss resilience.

items.title: Special Branch cop lodges fresh report over alleged assault by Shuhaily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Special Branch policeman who claims he was assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has lodged another police report to provide new evidence. Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin said their client, Lance Corporal Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, lodged the report at the Sungai Besi police station on Oct 10. The law firm alleged that Faiz and another lance corporal, Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, who serve as Travel Control Officers (TCO), were assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area.

items.title: Netanyahu demands probe into Gaza film's anonymous Israeli military sources
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Sunday for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in the award-winning Gaza war documentary "NAZA." The film is based on testimony from 24 unnamed Israeli military whistleblowers who accuse the army of killing numerous civilians in Gaza with the use of AI-powered targeting systems. "Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu this evening asked the chief of staff of the Israeli army, the head of the Shin Bet (domestic intelligence), and the state attorney to open a thorough investigation targeting the participants in the film 'NAZA' and to prosecute them," Netanyahu's office said in a statement.

items.title: #NSTViral: Two lorries destroyed, two factories damaged in Bukit Puchong fire [WATCH]
items.summary: PUCHONG: A fire in Bandar Bukit Puchong yesterday destroyed two lorries and damaged two factories. "The operations commander reported that the fire involved two factories," the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said in a statement issued at 7.10pm. "The fire also involved two lorries, which were 100 per cent burnt," the department said.

items.title: Lula stages mass rally ahead of Brazil's presidential run-off
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva led a massive rally Sunday to call for more days off for workers ahead of an election runoff against his right-wing opponent Flavio Bolsonaro. A sea of people massed along Sao Paulo's Paulista Avenue, which was awash in red, the color of Lula's Workers' Party. Polls show the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro is favoured to win the October 25 runoff.

items.title: Haze rebounds across 22 areas in Malaysia even as schools set to reopen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Air quality deteriorated across several states this morning, with 22 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as schools in multiple states prepared to resume physical classes. According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data as of 8.46am, only three stations recorded good air quality while 42 were in the moderate range. In Terengganu, elevated readings were recorded across Kemaman (157), Paka (156), and Kuala Terengganu (154).

items.title: Gold steady as markets strap in for US inflation data
items.summary: Spot gold steadied at US$4,200.23 per ounce by 0010 GMT after hitting a one-week high on Friday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.20 per cent to US$4,225.50. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.50 per cent to US$61.08, platinum added 0.40 per cent to US$1,693.51 and palladium climbed 0.70 per cent to US$1,155.84.

items.title: Two killed, five injured in Glenmarie crash
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Two 20-year-old men were killed and five others injured in a midnight crash involving a Proton Wira and a Proton Exora at the Hicom-Glenmarie Industrial Park. "Two of them, both aged 20, died at the scene, while the two 19-year-olds suffered minor injuries. "The Exora occupants - a 29-year-old woman and two men aged 27 and 28 - sustained minor injuries," he said.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar on fiscal discipline pledge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, supported by the government's commitment to fiscal discipline following the tabling of 2027 Budget last Friday. At 8am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0820/0880 against the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0830/0875. He said the pragmatic approach should help preserve Malaysia's sovereign credit rating, providing firm support for the ringgit.

items.title: PS the Children backs Budget 2027 digital safeguards, calls for transparent funding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Child advocacy group Protect & Save The Children Malaysia (PS the Children) has welcomed the child safety measures in Budget 2027, but urged the government to establish dedicated, transparent funding to guarantee their execution. The group commended the explicit recognition of online child sexual exploitation in the national budget speech, noting that the screen in a child's hands has become a primary staging ground for abuse. Key budget pledges include upgrading the police D11 division’s Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children (MICAC) system with advanced analytics, expanding the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s school safety campaigns, enforcing the Online Safety Act, and training 6,000 caregivers under a RM100 million matching grant.

items.title: IKEA Malaysia strengthens omnichannel strategy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IKEA Malaysia is evolving its retail approach as changing consumer behaviour and digital shopping reshape how Malaysians shop for home furnishings. IKEA Malaysia Country Retail Director Takeshi Murai said the upcoming Kuching store would reflect this approach. In Ipoh, consumers can order IKEA products and have them delivered to an IKEA collection point.

items.title: Oil climbs as Mideast conflict, tanker attacks persist
items.summary: Brent crude futures rose 76 cents, or 0.73 per cent, to US$105.48 a barrel by 2304 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$92.44 a barrel, up 59 cents, or 0.64 per cent. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to US$90 a barrel, up from US$85 previously, its analysts led by Daan Struyven said in a note.

items.title: UM MINT, IUCEL put AI-driven teaching, learning in focus
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The UM Mastery in Innovative Teaching (UM MINT) Colloquium and the International University Carnival on E-Learning (IUCEL) 2026 brought together 216 participants from 26 institutions to exchange ideas and innovative teaching practices. This made continuous innovation in teaching methods, assessment, student engagement and learning design increasingly important, she said. Hasniza said UM has an AI policy for teaching and learning.

items.title: Why strategic communication is becoming a leadership competency
items.summary: The employees applaud. Communication in an organisation no longer means simply transmitting information; it also means providing context to employees. Employees today don't just need information; they need context and meaning.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Make growth pay
items.summary: THE 2027 Budget 2027 carries a headline figure of RM510 billion. The budget offers meaningful relief within constrained public finances. Development expenditure rises from RM81 billion to RM83 billion.

items.title: SJPP guarantees RM123.8bil in business financing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) has facilitated RM123.81 billion in financing approvals for Malaysian businesses since 2009, reflecting continued demand for funding support among enterprises. For the January-August 2026 period, SJPP approved RM7.46 billion in financing involving 10,240 accounts. "These figures indicate continued financing demand among Malaysian businesses.

items.title: Emoluments, pensions drive higher govt operating spending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Higher emoluments, retirement charges and debt servicing are driving government operating expenditure 3.8 per cent higher to RM376.8 billion in 2027. Emoluments, the largest component of operating expenditure, are forecast to increase 2.9 per cent to RM111.6 billion next year from RM108.4 billion in 2026. Debt service charges are projected to increase 6.5 per cent to RM61 billion, representing 16.2 per cent of operating expenditure.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Consumers, property stocks in spotlight
items.summary: It named 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, MR DIY Group (M) Bhd, Leong Hup International Bhd and Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd among its top picks. MBSB Research favoured Mah Sing Group Bhd and Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd, while HLIB picked Matrix Concepts and SkyWorld Development Bhd. MBSB Research favoured Gamuda Bhd, Sunway Construction Group Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd, while RHB Research picked Gamuda, Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd and Sunway Construction.

items.title: Your MP resigned: What happens to their Malaysian constituencies?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — What happens to a Malaysian constituency when their Member of Parliament (MP) resigns? Wong resigned as Subang MP on August 10 after three terms in Parliament. Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung resigned after PKR suspended his membership for three years.

items.title: Temporary lane closures, diversions on Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway starting Oct 12 for elevated U-turn works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 11 — The rightmost lanes along both directions of the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway will be temporarily closed from October 12 to February 28, 2027, to facilitate the next phase of construction works for an elevated U-turn. IJM Land Berhad in a statement today said the closure would affect the median-side rightmost lanes of the George Town-bound and Bayan Lepas-bound carriageways. “The initial phase of construction for the elevated U-turn was successfully completed in early September, and upon completion, the elevated U-turn is expected to complement the Air Itam Bypass, helping to improve road connectivity and traffic flow along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway.

items.title: Sungai Golok river basin project: Scope, design adjustments aim to provide long-term flood protection
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 11 — Adjustments to the scope and design of the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin (PLSB) project in Kelantan are among the factors affecting its implementation timeline and cost. The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) said the adjustments were made to meet current needs, taking into account climate change, infrastructure requirements, actual site conditions and the needs of local residents. “Among the adjustments made were those involving land acquisition, changes to the project alignment and drainage system capacity to ensure that the project’s design and scope were suited to current conditions and that the flood mitigation system could function more effectively.

items.title: DPM Zahid to lead Malaysian delegation on five-day China working visit
items.summary: BEIJING, Oct 11 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will undertake a five-day working visit to China beginning tomorrow to strengthen bilateral ties, particularly in trade, investment, technology, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit, from October 12 to 16, would include a series of meetings with Chinese government leaders in Beijing before Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, travels to Tianjin to attend the World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference (WVTEDC) 2026. He said the agenda in Beijing would begin with a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, followed by a meeting with Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong and several engagements with trade companies to explore opportunities for economic cooperation.

items.title: MCMC boosts UMS internet coverage with 1,010 new Wi-Fi access points, says Teo Nie Ching
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has added approximately 1,010 Wi-Fi access points at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to expand internet coverage on the campus. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said that this initiative is part of MCMC’s ongoing efforts to ensure that the people of Sabah, particularly students and higher education institution (IPT) communities, have access to high-quality internet services. Teo said the addition will make internet coverage on the campus more comprehensive, thereby enhancing internet access convenience for the university community.

items.title: ‘Lighad’ issue: Quran must not be subject to mockery, says religious affairs minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The sanctity of the Quran must always be upheld as it serves as the ultimate source of divine guidance for Muslims, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said. He said mocking or insulting the Quran was an irresponsible act that could hurt the religious sensitivities of Muslims. Responding to the viral issue concerning the word “lighad”, which appears in Verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr, Zulkifli said the word meant “tomorrow” and had a contextual meaning pertaining to preparations for the Hereafter.

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine ready to halt refinery strikes if Russia stops hitting energy grid
items.summary: KYIV, Oct 11 — Ukraine would be ready to stop hitting Russian oil refineries if Russia curbed its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday, after criticism from US counterpart Donald Trump. Zelensky described the deal as a “weak decision”, saying it would encourage Russia to keep attacking Ukraine, but Trump said Saturday that Ukraine’s strikes were to blame for rising fuel prices. “Ukraine will be ready to stop striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure.

items.title: Two dead, including baby girl, in Gua Musang crash involving three cars and motorcycle
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 11 — Two people, including a baby girl, were killed in an accident involving three cars and a motorcycle on the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai Road, Kampung Paloh 3, here this afternoon. The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) stated in a release that the 5.10pm accident also resulted in seven other individuals being injured, including two who were reported to be in critical condition. According to the statement, the accident involved three Perodua Myvi cars and a Modenas motorcycle.

items.title: Wanita PKR lodges police report against Eric See-To over alleged mockery of Quranic verse
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 11 — Wanita PKR has lodged a police report against the owner of the Facebook account Eric See-To, also known as Lim Sian See, over a post allegedly mocking an expression related to a Quranic verse. Wanita PKR executive committee member Farahida Fauzi said the report was lodged at the Kuantan District Police Headquarters at about noon today to enable the matter to be investigated. Farahida, who is also Wanita PKR Pahang deputy chief, reminded the public not to make fun of religion to attract attention, provoke others or seek popularity.

items.title: Sarawak longhouse fire leaves 25 people homeless in Ulu Tinjar
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 11 — Three units of a longhouse at Rumah Wani in Ulu Tinjar were completely destroyed in a fire this morning, affecting three families comprising 25 people. “The fire involved three units of a longhouse built with non-permanent materials, namely units four, five and six, covering an estimated area of 54 by 100 feet. “All three units were completely destroyed,” Bomba said in a statement.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to unveil candidates on Oct 18, says Anwar’s aide
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will announce its candidates for the Melaka state election on October 18, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to personally unveil the line-up, said his political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin. Azman said the venue for the announcement would be announced at a later date. On speculation that he would contest the Paya Rumput seat in the election, Azman said he would leave the matter to the party leadership.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, N. Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya and parts of KL, Selangor to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow. In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days. In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.

items.title: Haze: Air quality in Kuching, Miri improves to moderate levels, says DOE
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 11 — Air quality in Kuching and Miri has improved but remains in the moderate category, according to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS) portal on Sunday. Kuching’s Air Pollutant Index (API) reading last recorded an unhealthy level at 2am today, at 111, before dropping to 99 at 3am. The reading subsequently declined from 153 at 3pm yesterday (Oct 10) to 85 at 3pm today, placing Kuching in the moderate category.

items.title: Digital tools, AI can preserve Dusun language for future generations, says Sabah deputy CM
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Digital technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), has the potential to become a crucial medium in efforts to preserve the Dusun language, ensuring that this community’s heritage continues to be learned, used, and inherited by future generations. Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said that modern technology can be leveraged through the development of digital dictionaries, recordings of Dusun speech, podcast production, and the creation of online learning materials. He noted that these efforts need to be strengthened through the involvement of the younger generation, educational institutions, and local communities so that the Dusun language remains relevant and continues to be used in daily life.

items.title: Budget 2027: Socso offers up to RM150 tax relief for Lindung 24 Jam, Lindung Kendiri contributors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Contributors who remain under the Lindung 24 Jam Scheme, as well as those making mandatory contributions to the Lindung Kendiri Scheme, will be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 under Budget 2027. The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), in a statement today, said the initiative is expected to benefit more than 8.5 million Lindung 24 Jam contributors and 1.7 million Lindung Kendiri contributors. Under Budget 2027, e-hailing and p-hailing workers will also receive a 35 per cent matching contribution from Perkeso, with the rate increasing to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute towards their social security payments.

items.title: Budget 2027: Nadma to use RM260m allocation for disaster relief centres, equipment, says Zahid
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) will prioritise the RM260 million allocated under Budget 2027 for establishing more Permanent Disaster Relief Centres (PPKBs) and procuring disaster preparedness assets and equipment, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. “We want to establish two permanent disaster relief centres in each state. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said this at a press conference after launching the 2026 National Preparedness Month (BKN) at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.

items.title: Health Ministry steps up efforts to recruit, retain nurses amid overseas migration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is expediting nurse recruitment and strengthening efforts to retain those already in service through improved welfare support and career advancement opportunities to address the migration of nurses abroad. Dzulkefly said other measures included maintaining the 42-hour working week for nurses on shift duty, expanding training and promotion opportunities, and offering greater flexibility in placements through a mutual exchange system. Dzulkefly said the MOH no longer recruited nurses on a contract basis, with all new recruits offered permanent appointments.

items.title: Pakatan targets Tampin parliamentary seat comeback in next GE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is aiming to reclaim the Tampin parliamentary seat at the next general election, with its election machinery urged to strengthen its efforts and engage voters from now. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said all parties must work harder to restore public confidence and demonstrate PH’s capabilities through its administrative performance and service to the community, Kosmo! Aminuddin, who is also Negeri Sembilan PH chairman, said winning back Tampin should be one of the coalition’s main priorities as it prepares for the general election, which is expected to be held in October or November next year.
